title: The Fake Mixtape
premise: Cyrus Voss, the only out kid in the dying town of Harrow Bend, has survived high school by keeping her head down and her best friend Deke's secrets closer than her own. When a college essay prompt — 'Describe a moment you betrayed someone' — circulates through the senior class, anonymous answers start leaking, and one of them exposes that Deke's star football season is built on a lie that could destroy him, the team, and Cyrus's own scholarship hopes. As the town hunts for who wrote what, Cyrus must decide whether loyalty means protecting Deke or telling the truth about what he did to her years ago. In the end she reads her real answer aloud at the last game of the season, losing Deke but winning herself.
about_author: Wendell Dunmore is a former small-town debate coach who spent a decade collecting the things teenagers almost said. He writes from a farmhouse where the nearest neighbor is a grain elevator.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Cyrus Voss narrates her carefully managed life in Harrow Bend: the gas station job, the tolerated-but-never-welcomed status as the only out kid in town, and her ironclad friendship with football captain Deke Marsh. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: brittle denial dressed up as contentment.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns a college essay: 'Describe a moment you betrayed someone.' The class goes silent; even the golden kids flinch. Cyrus realizes she has an answer she's never told anyone. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: a trapdoor opening under ordinary ground.

chapters.title: Deke's Version of Events
chapters.summary: At the quarry, Deke jokes about what he'd write — nothing, he says, he's never betrayed anybody. Cyrus swallows her own memory of sophomore year. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the cost of keeping peace measured in swallowed sentences.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Someone photographs the essay stack and posts answers anonymously to the school gossip account, one per day. The first leak guts a popular girl. The town lights up like a struck match. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: collective panic, voyeuristic thrill.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Suspects
chapters.summary: The principal cancels class discussions; parents demand the account be traced. Cyrus notices Deke checking his phone obsessively at practice. POV: alternating Cyrus and Deke. Emotional beat: paranoia turning neighbors into informants.

chapters.title: What Sophomore Year Cost
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the night Deke, drunk after a win, outed Cyrus in the locker room as a joke — then begged her to keep it quiet while he took credit for 'protecting' her. Her silence bought his stardom. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: old wound reopened, rage with nowhere to go.

chapters.title: Day Six
chapters.summary: A leaked essay hints that a 'star' betrayed someone close to him. The student body starts guessing; all eyes drift toward Deke. Cyrus realizes whoever leaks knows more than they should. POV: Deke. Emotional beat: the powerful discovering what powerlessness feels like.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Math
chapters.summary: Cyrus maps her escape route: the essay contest scholarship depends on faculty nomination, which depends on staying invisible. If the scandal touches her, she loses Harrow Bend forever. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: survival calculus that feels like cowardice.

chapters.title: Okafor's Office
chapters.summary: Ms. Okafor tells Cyrus she read every original essay before the leak — including Deke's, which describes betraying 'someone who never got to be angry about it.' She won't say whose. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: an adult offering truth like a lit match.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Cyrus teams with Priya Nair, the gossip account's reluctant admin, to trace the leaker before Deke's essay drops. Their uneasy alliance cracks when Priya admits she leaked the earlier ones for clout. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: complicity wearing the mask of justice.

chapters.title: The Last Normal Friday
chapters.summary: Pre-game bonfire. Deke gives a speech about brotherhood; the town cheers. Cyrus watches the boy who broke her get loved for the lie that covered it. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief for a friendship already half-dead.

chapters.title: Blackmail, Small Town Size
chapters.summary: Deke confronts Cyrus: he knows she was in Okafor's office, accuses her of leaking, threatens to tell everyone her 'real' essay is revenge porn of the past. POV: Deke. Emotional beat: fear curdling into cruelty — corruption in miniature.

chapters.title: The Essay Drops
chapters.summary: Deke's essay goes public: he confesses to betraying someone unnamed. The town rallies around him anyway — 'boys make mistakes.' Cyrus watches forgiveness get distributed by popularity. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of watching truth get rewritten.

chapters.title: Priya's Confession
chapters.summary: Priya reveals the final scheduled leak isn't hers — someone else has the account now, and the next post promises to name the person Deke betrayed. Countdown: the championship game. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: dread accelerating into freefall.

chapters.title: Who Knew
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Deke investigate together, old reflexes resurfacing. They discover the new leaker is Okafor's student teacher, who found the originals and wants to 'fix' the town. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: enemies forced into honesty by a worse threat.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: The student teacher offers Cyrus a deal: confirm the story anonymously and stay unharmed, or be named in the post. Deke begs her to take the deal — 'it protects us both.' POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the price of survival itemized in full.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Means
chapters.summary: Cyrus visits her mother's grave and finally says the sophomore-year story out loud to the headstone. She drafts her real college essay — the whole truth, names included. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the quiet moment courage actually happens.

chapters.title: Championship Eve
chapters.summary: The team's last practice. Deke apologizes without naming what he did — apology as strategy. Cyrus realizes he still doesn't understand, and maybe never will. POV: Deke. Emotional beat: remorse that stops just short of accountability.

chapters.title: The Last Game
chapters.summary: Halftime of the championship, the student teacher's post goes live — but it's garbled, anonymous, ignorable. Before the crowd disperses, Cyrus takes the mic during the senior recognition ceremony instead. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the cliff edge.

chapters.title: Her Answer
chapters.summary: Cyrus reads her essay aloud: what Deke did, what her silence cost, what betrayal really looks like in a town of nine hundred. The stadium goes silent; Deke walks off the field. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into release.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Population Nine Hundred
chapters.summary: The fallout: some kids thank her, some spit, the season ends in a loss nobody remembers. Deke doesn't speak to her. Okafor nominates her essay anyway. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the loneliness of doing the right thing.

chapters.title: The Acceptance Letter
chapters.summary: Spring: Cyrus gets in — with a scholarship note citing her essay's honesty. At the gas station, Deke buys coffee and says only, 'Good essay.' It isn't forgiveness, but it's a door left unlocked. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: hard-won, imperfect freedom.
